text:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered — sev2 — embed-service: error_rate >= 5% over 5m, routing fallback engaged.

Samira (oncall): seeing the same. I’m tracing requests now. KV-cache misses spiking.

Jun: heads-up — hit a small cohort of paying customers, some 500s and elevated tail latency. Customer impact metric: 0.8% of overall traffic but 3 customers with higher-than-usual errors.

Corey: I’m SSHing into the autoscaler dashboard. Looks like pods scaled down too aggressively after the midnight traffic dip. will bump min for embed pool.

Samira (oncall): mitigation plan — 1) scale embed-pool to 3 replicas 2) route affected traffic to fallback-variant (q4) 3) enable debug KV-cache logs for 10m. Doing step 1 now.

Corey: ran: 
```
kubectl scale deployment/embed-worker --replicas=3 -n inference
```
Scaling observed.

Samira (oncall): routing change applied: set route policy to prefer fallback-variant for requests > 8 tokens and from flagged customers. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

Priya (ProductQA): flagging the three customer accounts — sent secure notes to CS. They asked for ETA on fix.

Jun: quick ask — can we pin recent rollout to previous model build? I think the new build introduced heavier KV access patterns.

Corey: yes, can rollback if needed. I’m capturing a heap/profile dump and model-token distribution.

IncidentBot: Pager acknowledged by Samira (oncall).

Samira (oncall): logging captures look noisy — lots of concurrent KV fetch timeouts. Provisional hypothesis: a regression in the async KV client + autoscaler churn.

Ravi: I’m taking 30m handoff at :50. Current state: scaled, route fallback applied, debug logs on. No rollback yet. Customer comm draft needed. Anything else to add?

Samira (oncall): please monitor error rate and tail latency for the three flagged customers. If errors > 2% for them, escalate to SE and send interim comm. I’ll follow up in the post-handoff notes.

Ravi: acknowledged. I’ll set an alert threshold and hand it back at the 1h check. Also will attach the heap/profile artifacts to the incident.

Corey: creating short list of action items for postmortem:
- reproduce locally with KV client debug flags
- add a canary that exercises long-run KV patterns
- review autoscaler downscale threshold (owner: Corey, due: 2026-03-23)
- add request-level tagging for fallback routing events (owner: Jun, due: 2026-03-20)
- customer comm draft (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-19)

Priya (ProductQA): I’ll draft the comm and loop in CS and legal.

Samira (oncall): we should schedule a post-incident review this week. Proposed: Thurs 09:30 PT, 30m, include SRE, runtime, product, CS. I’ll own the notes and action tracking.

Ravi: works for me. I can present timeline and mitigation steps.

Jun: +1. Can we also do a short org brown-bag after the PIR to share prevention patterns? Maybe 4/1? I can put a calendar hold.

Samira (oncall): yes — brown-bag: 'KV cache resilience and autoscaler learnings' — 45m, include demo of new canary and quickfix playbook. Volunteers: Jun (demo), Corey (autoscaler changes), Priya (customer comms).

Corey: will add a short runbook snippet to infra repo: how to pin model build and apply fallback routing quickly. Example commands to include: 
```
# pin model
redwoodctl model pin embed-model:v2026-03-14
# apply route
redwoodctl route set embed-service --fallback=variant-q4
```

Samira (oncall): action tracker — I’ll open an incident board and add those items. Please add estimates and label owners. We’ll tie to the PIR ticket.

IncidentBot: Incident marked 'mitigated' at 1965432899. Postmortem required.

Priya (ProductQA): updating CS with interim comm now, will send final after PIR.

Ravi: handoff complete. I’ll monitor next 30m then close the circle. Thanks all.

Samira (oncall): thanks team. Postmortem invite and board link to follow in this thread. (reaction :eyes:)
